description:
A false-colour infrared satellite image illustrating land cover delineation for Copernicus Land Monitoring Service (CLMS) products, likely within a CORINE Land Cover (CLC) or High Resolution Layer (HRL) framework. The image uses a false-colour infrared (NIR-Red-Green) band combination, where deep blue/black areas represent water bodies, reddish-magenta areas indicate vegetation, and light blue/cyan/white areas show built-up surfaces and impervious features.

Multiple polygons are overlaid on the satellite imagery. A central, densely built-up area (light blue/cyan) is outlined by a light blue polygon. Within this delineated area, the numerical label "1400" is displayed in yellow text, indicating a land cover classification code. This central area appears to be an industrial or commercial complex, potentially including port infrastructure, situated adjacent to a large body of water. The light blue delineated area is fully enclosed by a larger, irregularly shaped yellow polygon, which itself is part of a broader network of yellow-outlined land parcels seen across the image, primarily encompassing vegetated areas. A thin yellow line, likely representing a road or linear infrastructure, traverses horizontally through the bottom third of the image.

The image is an example of land cover delineation, similar to examples cited for Avezzano (Italy), Uleforss (Norway), and Brevik (Norway). The imagery source is Spot 5 with 2.5 metre resolution, captured on 2011-08-15. Copyright CNES 2011©, Distribution Airbus DS/Spot Image.
